events.title: John's Vision of the Risen Christ
events.description: John is imprisoned on the island of Patmos for the word of God and the testimony of Jesus. On the Lord's Day, he is caught up in the Spirit and sees the risen Christ standing among seven golden lampstands, dressed in a long robe with a golden sash around his chest. His hair is white like wool, his eyes like blazing fire, and he holds seven stars in his right hand. John falls at his feet as though dead, but Christ lays his hand on him and says: "Do not be afraid! I am the First and the Last."

events.title: The Letter to Ephesus
events.description: The church in Ephesus is commended for its perseverance and for exposing false apostles, but criticized for having abandoned its first love. Christ urges them to repent and do the works they did at first, or else he will remove their lampstand.

events.title: The Letter to Smyrna
events.description: The church in Smyrna receives only encouragement and no criticism. Christ knows their affliction and poverty, yet says they are rich. He prepares them for persecution and imprisonment and urges them to remain faithful even unto death, so that they may receive the crown of life.

events.title: The Letter to Pergamum
events.description: The church in Pergamum lives where Satan's throne is, yet holds fast to Christ's name. Nevertheless, they are criticized for having people who hold to the teaching of Balaam and the teaching of the Nicolaitans. Christ threatens to come and fight against them with the sword of his mouth.

events.title: The Letter to Thyatira
events.description: The church in Thyatira is commended for its love, faith, service, and perseverance, but criticized for tolerating the woman Jezebel, who leads God's servants into sexual immorality and idolatry. Christ promises power over the nations to the one who conquers and holds fast to his works.

events.title: The Letter to Sardis
events.description: The church in Sardis has a reputation of being alive, but is dead. Christ urges them to wake up and strengthen what remains, which is about to die. A few in Sardis have not soiled their garments, and they will walk with him in white.

events.title: The Letter to Philadelphia
events.description: The church in Philadelphia has little strength, yet has kept Christ's word and not denied his name. Christ has set before them an open door that no one can shut, and promises to keep them from the hour of trial that is coming upon the whole world.

events.title: The Letter to Laodicea
events.description: The church in Laodicea is neither cold nor hot, but lukewarm. Christ threatens to spit them out of his mouth. They think they are rich, but are actually poor, blind, and naked. Christ stands at the door and knocks, promising fellowship with anyone who opens.

events.title: The Throne in Heaven
events.description: John sees an open door in heaven and is caught up in the Spirit. He sees God's throne surrounded by twenty-four elders dressed in white with crowns of gold, four living creatures full of eyes, and lightning and thunder. Everything that lives worships him who sits on the throne and sings: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty."

events.title: The Lamb and the Scroll
events.description: John sees a scroll with seven seals in the hand of the one sitting on the throne, but no one is worthy to open it. John weeps, but one of the elders comforts him: The Lion from the tribe of Judah has conquered. John sees a lamb that looked as if it had been slaughtered, with seven horns and seven eyes. The Lamb takes the scroll, and all heaven breaks out in praise.

events.title: The Six Seals Are Opened
events.description: The Lamb breaks the first six seals. The first four release four riders: the white horse brings conquest, the red one war, the black one famine, and the pale green one death. The fifth seal reveals the souls of martyrs under the altar crying out for justice. The sixth seal triggers a mighty earthquake; the sun becomes black and the moon like blood, and all people hide in caves among the mountains.

events.title: The 144,000 Are Sealed
events.description: Four angels hold back the winds over the earth while another angel rises with the seal of the living God. 144,000 from the tribes of Israel are sealed – 12,000 from each tribe. Then John sees an innumerable multitude from all nations standing before the throne, dressed in white robes, praising the Lamb. One of the elders explains that they have come out of the great tribulation.

events.title: The Seventh Seal and the First Four Trumpets
events.description: The Lamb breaks the seventh seal, and there is silence in heaven for about half an hour. Seven angels are given seven trumpets. When the first four trumpets sound, hail and fire mixed with blood strike the earth; a burning mountain is thrown into the sea; a great star named Wormwood falls and poisons the water sources; and one-third of the sun, moon, and stars are darkened.

events.title: The Fifth Trumpet – The First Woe
events.description: The fifth angel sounds his trumpet, and a star falls from heaven with the key to the bottomless pit. Smoke rises and darkens the sun, and from the smoke come locust-like creatures that torment people for five months. They have a king over them: the angel of the abyss, Abaddon. People seek death but do not find it.

events.title: The Sixth Trumpet – The Second Woe
events.description: The sixth angel sounds his trumpet, and four angels who had been bound at the great river Euphrates are released to kill a third of mankind. An army of two hundred million horsemen, with fire, smoke, and sulfur, kills a third of humanity. Yet the rest of mankind does not repent of their idols or their evil deeds.

events.title: The Two Witnesses
events.description: Two witnesses prophesy for 1260 days, clothed in sackcloth. They have power to shut the sky so that no rain falls, to turn water into blood, and to strike the earth with plagues. When they finish their testimony, the beast from the abyss kills them, and the whole world rejoices over their death. But after three and a half days, God breathes life into them, and they ascend to heaven in a cloud.

events.title: The Seventh Trumpet
events.description: The seventh angel sounds his trumpet, and loud voices in heaven proclaim: "The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ, and he shall reign forever and ever!" The twenty-four elders fall down and worship God. The temple of God in heaven is opened, and the ark of the covenant is seen, followed by lightning, thunder, an earthquake, and great hail.

events.title: The Woman and the Dragon
events.description: A great sign appears in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars on her head. She is about to give birth, but a great red dragon with seven heads and ten horns stands ready to devour her child as soon as it is born. The child is caught up to God, and the woman flees into the wilderness. Michael and his angels fight against the dragon and cast him down to the earth. The dragon pursues the woman, but the earth helps her.

events.title: The Beast from the Sea
events.description: John sees a beast rising out of the sea with ten horns and seven heads, and on its horns were ten crowns. The dragon gives the beast his power, his throne, and great authority. One of its heads seemed to have received a fatal wound that was healed, and the whole earth marveled and followed the beast. It is given power to make war against the saints for 42 months and to rule over every tribe, people, language, and nation.

events.title: The Beast from the Earth and the Mark of the Beast
events.description: Another beast rises out of the earth with two horns like a lamb, but it speaks like a dragon. It performs great signs and deceives those who live on the earth, causing them to worship the first beast. It forces all people to receive a mark on their right hand or forehead so that they can buy or sell. The number of the beast is the number of a man: 666.

events.title: The Lamb on Mount Zion
events.description: John sees the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with him are the 144,000 who have the name of the Lamb and the name of his Father written on their foreheads. They sing a new song before the throne that no one else can learn. Three angels proclaim: the eternal gospel to all nations, the fall of Babylon, and a warning against worshiping the beast or receiving its mark.

events.title: The Seven Bowls of Wrath
events.description: Seven angels carrying the seven last plagues come out of the temple in heaven. They pour their bowls over the earth: painful sores break out on people, the sea and rivers turn to blood, the sun scorches people with fire, the kingdom of the beast is plunged into darkness, the Euphrates dries up to prepare the way for the kings from the east, and finally, the greatest earthquake ever occurs, splitting Babylon into three parts and causing cities to collapse.

events.title: The Great Harlot Babylon
events.description: One of the seven angels shows John the great harlot sitting by many waters. She sits on a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns, clothed in purple and scarlet, adorned with gold and precious stones. On her forehead is written a mysterious name: "Babylon the Great, mother of prostitutes and of all abominations on earth." She is drunk with the blood of the saints.

events.title: The Fall of Babylon
events.description: A mighty angel cries out with a loud voice: "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great!" All the kings of the earth and merchants who grew rich from her weep and mourn over her destruction. An angel lifts a stone like a great millstone and throws it into the sea as a sign that Babylon will be thrown down and never found again. A voice from heaven calls God's people to come out of her.

events.title: The Marriage Supper of the Lamb
events.description: A great multitude in heaven cries "Hallelujah!" and praises God because he has judged the great harlot and avenged the blood of his servants. A voice from the throne says: "Let us rejoice and be glad and give him glory! For the time has come for the marriage of the Lamb, and his bride has made herself ready." The bride has been granted to wear fine linen, bright and pure, which represents the righteous acts of the saints.

events.title: The Rider on the White Horse
events.description: Heaven opens, and John sees a white horse. Its rider is called "Faithful and True," his eyes are like blazing fire, and he wears many crowns. He is clothed in a robe dipped in blood, and his name is "the Word of God." The armies of heaven follow him on white horses. He strikes down the nations with a sharp sword and treads the winepress of God's wrath. The beast and the false prophet are thrown alive into the lake of fire.

events.title: The Thousand-Year Reign
events.description: An angel seizes the dragon, that ancient serpent who is the devil and Satan, and binds him for a thousand years. He is cast into the abyss, which is sealed over him. Those who had held fast to their testimony about Jesus and had not worshiped the beast are raised to life and reign with Christ for a thousand years. When the thousand years are ended, Satan will be released for a short time.

events.title: The Final Judgment
events.description: John sees a great white throne and the one seated on it. Earth and heaven flee from his presence. The dead, great and small, stand before the throne, and books are opened. Another book is opened, the book of life. The dead are judged according to what was written in the books, by their deeds. Death and Hades are thrown into the lake of fire, and anyone whose name is not found written in the book of life is also thrown into the lake of fire.

events.title: A New Heaven and a New Earth
events.description: John sees a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and there was no longer any sea. He sees the new Jerusalem coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. A loud voice from the throne says: "Look! God's dwelling place is now among the people. He will dwell with them, and they will be his people. God himself will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more."

events.title: The New Jerusalem
events.description: An angel shows John the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven in God's glory. The city shines like a most precious jewel, has twelve gates with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, and twelve foundations bearing the names of the apostles. The city is built of pure gold, clear as glass, and needs neither sun nor moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gives it light. The river of life flows from the throne of God and of the Lamb, and the tree of life bears fruit twelve times a year.

events.title: Jesus' Promise to Come Soon
events.description: The angel confirms that the words of this book are trustworthy and true. Jesus says: "See, I am coming soon! Blessed is the one who keeps the prophetic words of this book." John is urged not to seal up the prophetic words of the book, for the time is near. The book concludes with an earnest prayer: "Come, Lord Jesus!" and a blessing of grace upon all the saints.
